answer: Ephemeral Work Ledger. Each identity must complete a small paid task whose output is logged to a rolling record; payment unlocks only after the record clears. Cloning means funding a fresh identity and redoing that work per clone, while a real operator pays it once and reuses the quill of accumulated history. A clone therefore pays the full task price plus the delay each time, and repeated clones drain capital faster than any single honest account. The zenith of profit stays with the account that keeps one stable ledger position, and a cedar of shared work history anchors that advantage.
